title: WV Paranormal Trail returns in 2026 with a new addition
excerpt: West Virginia has its fair share of spooky locations, and the State Tourism Department is giving you a chance to explore them all one by one.
content:
CLARKSBURG, W.Va. (WBOY) — West Virginia has its fair share of spooky locations, and the State Tourism Department is giving you a chance to explore them all one by one.

On Thursday, the West Virginia Department of Tourism announced the return of its popular West Virginia Paranormal Trail, which launched in 2024 and features 20 “hair-raising locations” across the Mountain State for people to visit.

Those who travel along the trail can register online to receive a free digital passport that tracks each location you visit via check-ins.

New to the trail this year is Droop Mountain Battlefield State Park in Pocahontas County, a Civil War Battlefield that has been turned into a State Park.

While thrilling visits to some of West Virginia’s most-haunted places might be enough for some, the tourism department has also kicked in some incentives for people who visit many or all of the locations.

The following rewards are available for those who visit a set number of locations:

  • Visiting three or more locations gets you a glow-in-the-dark sticker
  • Visiting eight or more locations gets you a custom beanie
  • Visiting 15 or more spots gets you an adventure-ready lantern
  • Visiting every location gets you a limited-edition poster

Make sure to check in at each location you’re visiting in order for it to count toward your prizes. Those who visit every location will also be eligible to win the grand prize of an overnight tour for two at the Trans-Allegheny Lunatic Asylum in Weston. The winner will be announced in January 2027.
